newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN TAKES COMMANDING NINE-SHOT LEAD AT TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN TAKES COMMANDING NINE-SHOT LEAD AT TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: British Open champion Tom Lehman turned the Tour Championship into a romp on Saturday by shooting a six-under-par 64 to open up a massive nine-stroke lead at Southern Hills.
Lehman finished at 13-under-par 197. A distant second was Vijay Singh, whose 69 left him at four under along with Brad Faxon, who shot a four-under 66.
Lehman, whose nine-stroke, 54-hole lead was the biggest on the PGA Tour since Jack Nicklaus led the King Island Open in 1973, positioned himself to sweep the year-end awards.
Victory should bring Lehman the money title, the Vardon trophy for low scoring average and PGA Player of the Year.
Lehman ranked his six-birdie performance at Southern Hills on Saturday as one of the best rounds of his career.

"It was one of those days when everything went right," said Lehman. "Sometimes you get that feeling that you know exactly where the ball is going. Today was one of those days, if you told me to hit it 109 yards, I'd hit it 109."

Singh, who played with Lehman, could only say, "it was fun watching Tom today. He was doing everything correct, and putting great. I don't think there's much chance for any of us to catch him if he keeps playing the way he has been."
Lehman, who says that confidence was always the toughest element of the game for him to master, was able to feel comfortable about his position.
"If I go out and play my game tomorrow, it's going to be extremely tough, maybe impossible, for anyone to pick up nine shots," Lehman said.

"I learned at the British that you have to stick to your game plan. You can't afford to back off at all. It's sometimes difficult with a big lead to get into that aggressive mindset, it's too easy to try to protect what you have. But I would say I'm an aggressive player, and for me to play cautiously is probably unwise."

Although Lehman came into this week feeling optimistic abou his game and his chances, the pre-tournament attention was on Tiger Woods, who ended the third round with a double bogey on the 18th for a 72 and a 10-over 220 total, 23 strokes behind Lehman.
Woods's father, Earl, who was hospitalized here in the early morning hours of Friday, is still in hospital, but according to Tiger, is feeling much better.

The Woods family is being guarded about his condition, but apparently chest pains sent the elder Woods, who had bronchitis, into St. Francis' emergency room and fluid was reportedly found in his lungs.
Said Tiger on Saturday, "Yesterday was a day where I was thinking about my dad all day, but today I knew the situation was under control, so I felt I could come out and focus on my game."
